The reported faithfulness metrics cannot distinguish 'templated but correct' from 'templated and wrong about the behaviour'. See few_shot_count_experiment.

Thai-language qualitative review by a human reader is still not done, and variant C shows why no script here can substitute for it.

priority_rule.rule: fused_prediction != 1 -> LOW; fused_score >= 0.80 -> HIGH; otherwise MEDIUM
priority_rule.inputs: fused_score and fused_prediction only; rf confidence is not used because it measures RF certainty in either direction, not attack risk
priority_rule.status: provisional: chosen to match the five tests/fixtures expectations, not tuned on data or validated with analysts

m2_measurement.status: measured on 100 alerts on the UNIFIED population (the deployed pipeline)
m2_measurement.evidence: reports/llm_faithfulness_raw.jsonl (one line per alert; every rate is recomputable from it)
m2_measurement.sample: 100 alerts, seed 42, stratified over 14 CICIDS-2017 attack categories (capped at 7 each so DoS Hulk and DDoS cannot dominate) plus 10 BENIGN. Per-category rates rest on 2-7 alerts and are descriptive only, not natural-traffic rates.
m2_measurement.pipeline: the real deployed path per alert: the three *_unified models on one 94-feature population, fuse_with_metadata (confidence_weighted cascade), RagRetriever.retrieve(top_k=3) queried with the RF predicted label, then llm_explain.explain_alert.

results.gen_speed: ~60-67 tok/s on the RTX 3070, ~5.8 s/alert, no corrective retries needed

m2_measurement.supersedes: the earlier 100-alert run, which scored random_forest.pkl (80 features) plus the behavioral_v2 IF/AE (92 features) reconciled by a row-hash join, and recorded model_used as 'autoencoder_v2' -- a value fusion_layer no longer emits. Those figures described a pipeline that is not deployed and must not be cited. Preserved as reports/llm_faithfulness_*.before_fewshot_fix.*
m2_measurement.configuration: two rendered few-shot examples, `confidence` removed from FACTS (variant B)

problem_history: Realistic example values were copied into outputs in 30/100 alerts, one near-verbatim.

Replacing them with {{...}} placeholders was meant to leave nothing plausible to copy. The model copied the placeholders themselves, so the entity guard rejected 100% of alerts: a total outage, worse than the leak. An instruction telling the model not to copy had already failed, and an instruction that has already failed is not a control.
few_shot_leak_control.root_fix: llm_explain.render_few_shots substitutes each placeholder with THIS alert's own values before the examples reach the prompt. There is no generic token left to copy, so a copied value is the correct value for that alert, and the example still demonstrates that entities must be named rather than omitted.
few_shot_leak_control.guard_retained: llm_explain._assert_no_foreign_entities still rejects any IPv4, hostname-shaped token or Txxxx id absent from FACTS, with one corrective retry then ValueError. It fails loudly on purpose: an explanation naming the wrong host sends an analyst to the wrong machine.
few_shot_leak_control.cost_measured: the risk it traded into is template echoing, and it is large: 60/100 explanations are >=0.80 similar to a rendered example and 51/100 are verbatim copies. This is measured by the example_echo metric rather than assumed away.

confidence_field_removed.problem: `confidence` is the fusion rule's own |P(attack) - 0.5| * 2 -- certainty in EITHER direction, high both when the model is sure it IS an attack and sure it is NOT. The explanation layer read it as certainty-of-attack and wrote 'ความมั่นใจต่ำ (0.99)' on benign rows: correct number, backwards reading.
confidence_field_removed.scale: 12/100 alerts, and it PASSED the mechanical claim check because the number is right
confidence_field_removed.found_by: running src/pipeline.py end to end -- the seam is between fusion and the explanation layer, so neither component's own tests could see it
confidence_field_removed.fix: removed from FACTS entirely rather than renamed, because a renamed ambiguous quantity is still ambiguous and fused_score already carries risk in one direction. The prompt now forbids quoting a numeric confidence at all and asks for severity to be conveyed through priority. Note the file's own comment already said this value was 'not used because it is RF certainty in either direction' while the code passed it in twice.
confidence_field_removed.effect: 12/100 -> 0/100, and no explanation mentions model confidence at all
confidence_field_removed.cost: entity_complete 100/100 -> 94/100 and hallucination 1.91% -> 2.94%. Reported rather than omitted: the fix is a trade, not a free win.

few_shot_count_experiment.question: does reducing the few-shot examples from two to one reduce template echoing?
few_shot_count_experiment.answer: no -- it makes it total, and the faithfulness metrics reward that
few_shot_count_experiment.why_C_was_rejected_despite_perfect_score: With one template to match, the model fills it in and does nothing else. All 100 explanations describe the flow as 'ส่งคำขอผิดรูปแบบจำนวนมาก' (sending many malformed requests) -- including all 10 BENIGN flows, where it is false. Two examples: the phrase appears on 52/100 and on ZERO benign flows.
few_shot_count_experiment.what_this_exposes_about_M2: A BLIND SPOT, and it is the most important result of this experiment. M2 checks that named entities match the alert and that technique ids are grounded. It cannot check whether the described BEHAVIOUR matches the attack type, so prose that is entity-perfect and semantically wrong scores 1.0000 on every axis. Selecting a configuration by maximising M2 would have chosen the degenerate one. This is why the human Thai-language review is not optional.
